title: Schema rollback and fallback protocol for typed streams (PRD draft)
content:
Status: DRAFT — high-level engineering and product spec. Notes and examples below are intentionally informal.

Summary
This doc proposes a compact protocol and SDK ergonomics for: 1) negotiating typed/structured streaming outputs between client and Hosted API, 2) detecting and automatically rolling back to compatible output shapes when live validation fails or quality/regression signals appear, and 3) surface telemetry and developer controls for safe failover. Focus is on making structured schemas reliable in low-latency streaming and tool-calling scenarios while avoiding developer surprise when models drift or edge cases break schemas.

Motivation / problem statement
- Teams want to rely on typed outputs (JSON, typed frames, action schemas) to wire downstream systems and tools. In streaming scenarios, a single schema violation mid-stream can break downstream processors or tool calls (eg, DB writes, RPCs).
- Model updates (new checkpoints, quantization, reruns on different hardware) occasionally change tokenization/formatting behavior in ways that break schema validators.
- Current fallback behavior (return a plain text error or full failure) is developer-hostile, often requiring manual intervention or retries.

Goals
- Define a deterministic client-server handshake to advertise preferred schema, acceptable fallbacks, and version pins.
- Provide an automatic, observable rollback/fallback policy that preserves availability (avoid total failure) and minimizes silent data corruption.
- Make SDK ergonomics simple: explicit opt-in for strict vs best-effort schema enforcement, hooks for on-fallback callbacks, and clear telemetry.
- Ensure rollbacks are safe for tool-calling flows (avoid invoking external systems with malformed payloads).

Non-goals
- This doc does not redesign the entire streaming wire protocol. We assume the existing compact frame stream and incremental output mechanisms remain.
- This is not a full eval regimen for schema fidelity — that will live in Optimize/evals.

Key concepts and definitions
- Typed frame: a streaming message with a declared schema id and an incremental patch (e.g., partial JSON AST or typed action frame).
- Schema pin: a semantic version or model-verified shape attached to a session indicating the expected structure (eg, product.v1.2).
- Fallback mode: one of {strict-fail, best-effort-typed, untyped-text, tool-skip}.

Handshake and negotiation (high level)
Client -> POST /v1/stream?schema=product.v1.2&fallback=best-effort-typed
  Headers: X-Client-Schema-Preference: strict|best-effort
  Body: session metadata, allowed model variants, latency SLO
Server -> stream first frame includes: schema-ack: accepted|deferred|rejected; schema-version: product.v1.2 (or null); allowed-fallbacks: [untyped-text, tool-skip]
If schema-ack is deferred, server will attempt typed streaming but mark every typed frame with provisional:true until a validation window closes (eg, first commit frame success).

Rollback triggers (automatic)
- Live validation failure rate exceeds threshold (eg, >5% invalid frames in 1000 frames).
- Downstream safety check: tool-call payload validator rejects the commit payload.
- Latency SLO breaches that are tied to validation/repair heuristics.
- Manual rollback request from console or SDK control-plane API.

Rollback policy semantics
- Policy order (example default): strict-fail -> (if disabled) best-effort-typed -> untyped-text -> tool-skip
- When moving from typed -> untyped-text, the server will emit a special transition-frame: {"type":"schema_fallback","from":"product.v1.2","to":"untyped-text","reason":"validation_spike"} and mark following frames as untyped.
- Clients may opt into a buffered-hold mode: on fallback, hold final commit until SDK user inspects the produced text and explicitly re-commit. Useful for tool-calling where side effects are irreversible.

SDK ergonomics and API sketches
- High-level (pseudocode JavaScript):
  const stream = client.stream({schema: 'product.v1.2', fallback: 'best-effort-typed', strict: false});
  stream.on('typed-frame', (frame) => { /* safe to map to shape */ });
  stream.on('schema_fallback', (info) => { /* show dev banner / call onFallback handler */ });
  stream.on('untyped-chunk', (text) => { /* fallback content — developer decides what to do */ });
  await stream.commit({doToolCall: true, requireTyped: true}); // commit rejects if not typed and requireTyped==true
- Languages: JS/TS SDK will be primary for developer ergonomics; we will expose same hooks for Python/Go.
- SDK default: best-effort-typed, warn on fallback. Default should avoid silently invoking external tools with malformed payloads — commit APIs should have explicit flags to allow tool calls on fallback.

Tool-calling safety modes
- Safe-guard patterns: commit(requireTyped=true) will fail if session has fallen back. commit(requireTyped=false, allowToolSkip=true) will proceed but skip any tool invocation declared unsafe.
- Server-side: separate code path for tool execution that re-validates payloads before any external side-effects. If invalid, return tool_error and optionally enqueue a human-review ticket.

Observability and telemetry
- Emit structured events: schema_negotiation, schema_validation_failure (per-frame), schema_fallback, schema_rollback_trigger, commit_blocked_by_fallback.
- Console should show per-session schema health: validity rate, last fallback timestamp, fallback reason, and counts of blocked tool calls.
- Billing: document token cost differentials when fallback uses text-only reparsing or additional repair tokens.

Backward compatibility matrix
- Client opts strict:true and server lacks schema negotiation -> server returns rejected upfront and client can fall back to untyped streaming.
- Older SDKs without on('schema_fallback') will still receive the transition-frame as a chunked text event; we must keep a human-readable fallback notice at stream start to avoid silent failures.

Migration plan and rollout
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood): default best-effort-typed for internal infra teams, strict opt-in off.
- Phase 1 (beta): public SDKs expose fallback hooks and requireTyped commit flag; invite 10 customers to opt into schema pinning.
- Phase 2 (GA): enable schema health telemetry in Console, recommended rollout docs and failure action templates.

Operational runbook (short)
- On high validation failure rates: automatically throttle schema-heavy models and open an incident ticket to Model Onboarding and Applied ML to diagnose.
- If rollback due to tool-safety: notify solutions-eng and block further external executions until review.

Edge cases and examples
- Partial JSON streams: server may stream partial AST nodes. Validation must tolerate incremental frames that are not full JSON until the commit frame. Validator behavior: allow temporary syntactic incompleteness if incremental flag true.
- Stale schema pin: when client requires product.v1.2 but server only offers product.v1.1, server returns schema-ack: rejected plus nearest-compatible list; client SDK should provide automatic patching suggestions for PD.

Open questions / TODOs
- Threshold numbers for automatic rollback (operationally tuned).
- UX for console to allow manual N-day rollback vs immediate revert.
- Specific event schema for telemetry (payload size, tokens used during validation repairs).
- Evaluate model-level vs session-level vs request-level schema pins.

Security and privacy
- Schema payloads and validators may disclose small amounts of user data in logs; ensure validators support redaction and PII masking.
- Tool-skip vs untyped-text: default should favor data safety (do not call external tools with untrusted/unvalidated content).

Appendix: example transition frame (human-readable chunk to preserve compatibility with old SDKs)
{"note":"SCHEMA FALLBACK: product.v1.2 -> untyped-text; reason=validation_spike; timestamp=2025-09-12T14:22:03Z"}

Appendix: quick dev checklist
- Add schema_fallback event to StreamingTelemetry pipeline.
- SDK: add stream.on('schema_fallback') and stream.commit(requireTyped) flag.
- Console: add per-session schema health card and ability to force-rollback sessions.
- Infra: add rate limiter to typed-validate path to avoid cascading latency spikes.

Rough milestone timeline
- 2w: API handshake spec and SDK hooks landed (internal).
- 4w: Dogfood + telemetry ingestion.
- 8w: Beta with 3 customers and runbooks.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments
- Might want an intermediate "repair-frame" where the server emits a best-effort corrected typed payload and a confidence score. Avoid auto-accepting repairs without client opt-in.
- Consider a lightweight changelog for schema pins that surfaces small diffs so SDKs can auto-adapt in a safe way.

People to loop in
- Applied ML (model-onboarding), Serving Runtime (validation performance), SDK leads (JS/Python), Solutions Eng for tool-safety.

END DRAFT
